questions.stem: Soon after vaccination, an adult develops sudden wheezing and hypotension without urticaria. Anaphylaxis is suspected. Which immediate medication decision is most appropriate?

options.text: Wait for a rash before treating anaphylaxis
Use an oral antihistamine as the initial and sole treatment
Observe without medication because skin findings are absent

questions.explanation: Anaphylaxis may occur without urticaria. Suspected anaphylaxis with respiratory or cardiovascular involvement requires immediate intramuscular epinephrine; absence of a rash is not a reason to delay treatment.

questions.stem: An unvaccinated adult has a transdermal dog bite. While urgent referral for rabies prophylaxis is arranged, which local first-aid measure should begin immediately?

options.text: Leave the wound unwashed until referral
Rinse for a few seconds only
Wash thoroughly with soap and water for at least 15 minutes
Apply a dry covering without cleansing

questions.explanation: Start thorough soap-and-water washing immediately for at least 15 minutes. Washing does not replace vaccine or indicated wound infiltration with rabies immunoglobulin or monoclonal antibodies for category III exposure.
